editorial:
Imagine waking up in a perfect 1950s town where every house looks the same and your only job is to be a happy housewife. That is exactly where you find Alice and Jack. At first, it looks like a dream come true with sunny skies and fancy clothes, but you quickly realize something is off. Alice starts seeing weird things that do not make sense, and the more she asks questions, the more her husband and the other neighbors try to shut her down. It feels like a creepy game of pretend where one wrong move could ruin everything.

Florence Pugh is amazing here and really carries the movie with her acting. The twist is a wild ride, though some parts of the story feel a bit slow before the big reveal. If you love movies that make you question what is real, you will dig this.
endingExplained: You find out that the whole town is actually a virtual reality simulation. The men paid to put their wives in this fake world to control them. Alice was the only one who resisted and kept waking up. In the end, Alice fights her way out of the simulation and wakes up in the real world. She manages to escape the men and the machine, finally gaining her freedom back in the real life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves twisty mysteries and psychological thrillers.
